A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Compositional Risk Minimization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on six benchmarks, bias/prior ablations, and a numerical affine-hull membership experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds baseline evaluations, five-attribute CelebA results, and Gaussian classification simulations.

M1.justification: The proposed additive-energy classifier, joint likelihood objective, bias extrapolation, prior adjustment, and marginalization remain unchanged. The generalized pseudocode and additional attribute heads instantiate v1's existing m-attribute formulation; the original two-attribute algorithm moves to Appendix C.

E1.justification: The six original benchmarks remain. v2 adds five-attribute CelebA coverage using eyeglasses, hats, and earrings alongside hair color and gender, producing 32 groups (G.3). It also adds Gaussian classification scenarios, including settings with seven to nine attributes (Appendices E and G.6).

E2.justification: v1 evaluates ERM, G-DRO, LC, and sLA. v2 additionally evaluates IRM, VREx, and Mixup in the corresponding compositional-shift and standard benchmark comparisons (Tables 5–11 and 14), substantially expanding the comparator families.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics, backbones, and hyperparameter grids remain. New protocols include leave-one-group-out evaluation over 32 CelebA groups, pooling four spurious attributes into a 16-valued attribute for baselines, and controlled 100-dimensional Gaussian experiments varying attribute counts, category counts, and training-group retention (G.3 and G.6).

E4.justification: The original bias/prior ablations are retained. v2 adds Gaussian decision-boundary case studies comparing CRM and ERM (Figures 2 and 7) and extensive sensitivity analysis of training-group coverage (Figures 8–9). v1's separate random affine-hull membership experiment in Table 12 is removed.

E5.justification: Benchmark reporting retains means and standard errors over three seeds. v1's separate 1,000-run affine-hull frequency estimation is removed; v2's new predictive-simulation curves report three-seed means and standard errors. These are different experiments, not a stated reduction in repetitions for retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline and simulation results, including five-attribute CelebA WGA of 63.2 for CRM versus 34.3 for LC (Table 12). Retained reports also change: MultiNLI CRM WGA becomes 58.7 from 57.7 in Table 1, while CivilComments CRM WGA when dropping (1,7) becomes 63.0 from 65.0. Several ablation estimates also change.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the general-m conjectural treatment with a hull-growth proof giving O(md + d log d) scaling (Theorem 3 and D.4), and adds additive-function extrapolation reasoning in D.7. The two-attribute proof is retained in D.3. The new statements contain a consistency defect: Theorem 8 omits the factor c used in Theorem 7.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: additive-energy CRM enables discriminative compositional generalization within discrete affine hulls and improves robustness. The new theory and experiments strengthen support without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the additions as showing larger advantages with multiple spurious attributes and good synthetic generalization at 20% or 10% group retention. Existing bias/prior interpretations and affine-hull restrictions remain. G.3's added balanced-accuracy superiority claim conflicts with Table 12: CRM scores 90.1 versus 91.7 for LC and sLA.

D1.justification: v2 adds a PyTorch-style implementation covering priors, logits, bias extrapolation, and training/testing (C.2), plus attribute-coding and Gaussian-generation details (G.3 and G.6). These substantially expand documentation beyond v1's pseudocode and training settings. The listing contains discrepancies with the equations, including summing logits rather than probabilities during inference.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hinton (2002), Krueger et al. (2021), Zhang et al. (2017), and Bayat et al. (2025). Appendices B and D.7 refine the relationship to additive decoders and newly position the hull analysis as providing sharper characterization and sample bounds than Dong and Ma. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 shortens and moves related work near the end, edits the abstract and mathematical motivation, and replaces the detailed main algorithm with an overview while relocating the original to Appendix C. Most existing theoretical and experimental exposition is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds decision-boundary Figures 2 and 7, sensitivity Figures 8–9, and new aggregate and multi-attribute tables. Existing comparison tables gain baseline rows, and the compact CivilComments table is split into Tables 10–11. Original hull illustrations are retained and renumbered; v1's numerical hull table is removed.

improvement.justification: The general-m proof advances v1's conjecture and numerical check, while broader baseline comparisons, five-attribute CelebA, and controlled group-coverage experiments address important validation gaps. These substantially strengthen theoretical and empirical support. The gains outweigh new consistency problems, including mismatched theorem constants, the Table 12 balanced-accuracy overclaim, and errors in the implementation listing.
